overview.text: A submarine is a self-propelled watercraft designed to travel and operate underwater for extended periods. Its ballast tanks take in water to help it dive; compressed air expels that water to help it rise, while ballast adjustments and diving planes control depth and trim. Because its hull is windowless, a periscope can give the crew a limited view of the surface, though sonar and electronic sensors are also vital. Submarines have mattered as naval vessels and as vehicles for exploring the undersea world. They should not be confused with many small research submersibles, which make short excursions from a support ship.

key_facts.text: Flooding ballast tanks adds water and helps a submarine submerge; blowing water out with compressed air helps it surface.
Ballast adjustments and diving planes help control a submarine’s depth and trim while it is underwater.
A periscope provides a limited view outside the otherwise windowless hull; modern submarines also use sonar and electronic sensors.
Sonar lets a submarine detect sounds or echoes underwater, without needing to rise to periscope depth.
Submarines have served naval purposes and helped people explore underwater; many small research submersibles instead make short excursions from a support ship.
